What this pool holds constant

DimensionAcross the pooled cohortsIf it differs, why it is crossed anyway
effect measureESTABLISHEDboth stored as odds ratios derived from arm counts, on the log scale
estimandNOT ESTABLISHED, AND CHECKEDCHECKED ON 2026-08-20 AND FAILED, which is a different state from the 'not recorded on the page this object was extracted from' this field carried before -- that was the NEVER-CHECKED state written as though it were a negative finding. It has now been checked. JUPITER registers a FIVE-component composite: 'Time to Major Cardiac Event (Cardiovascular Death, Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, Hospitalization Due to Unstable Angina or Arterial Revascularization)'. HOPE-3 registers TWO co-primaries, 'The composite of; Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke.' and 'The composite of; cardiovascular death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, heart failure, arterial revascularizations'. Neither is JUPITER's. JUPITER counts any stroke and any myocardial infarction where both HOPE-3 composites count non-fatal only; JUPITER counts hospitalisation for unstable angina and neither HOPE-3 composite does; HOPE-3's second adds resuscitated cardiac arrest and heart failure, which JUPITER's does not. Three, five and six components with no containment ordering between them.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML0.6561 (0.484 to 0.8894)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.6561 (0.0913 to 4.7135)

The published point is 0.6561 and the house-rule point is 0.6561. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.

Title and review question

Time to Major Cardiac Event (Cardiovascular Death, Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, Hospitalization Due to Unstable Angina1

This object described its population as 'Adults with stroke'. that is wrong and it is WITHDRAWN. Both contributing trials are Primary prevention in people WITHOUT established cardiovascular disease. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-21: NCT00239681 is JUPITER, registered under the single condition 'Elevated high-sensitivity C-Reactive Protein (hsCRP)'; NCT00468923 is HOPE-3, an intermediate-risk primary-prevention trial. And the origin of the error is identifiable: hope-3's registry `conditions` array reads Cardiovascular Disease and Stroke because stroke is an OUTCOME it counts, not because its participants had one. A conditions field lists what a trial is about, which is not the same as what its participants have, and reading it as a population label turns an endpoint into a diagnosis. The correct description is: adults without established cardiovascular disease, at elevated risk. No estimate changes.2

In adults with stroke, does Rosuvastatin compared with placebo affect the outcome each trial registered as its primary, which differ across the 2 trials here?3

Results

The pooled odds ratio for time to Major Cardiac Event (Cardiovascular Death, Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, Hospitalization Due to Unstable Angina was 0.656 (0.484 to 0.889) across 2 trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from.1

THIS POOL IS REFERRED, NOT WITHDRAWN. The pooled odds ratio 0.6561 (0.484 to 0.8894) averages JUPITER's five-component composite with one of HOPE-3's two co-primaries, and the object cannot say which. This is the estimand-mixing shape that caused sglt2-hf's k=4 pool to be withdrawn.2

The trials' results were poorly consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 80.2%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.0387, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 5.04, on degrees of freedom 1. not recorded on the page this object was extracted from3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they SHOULD have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-20. Query, counts and the per-record disposition are in ssot/rosuvastatin-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 114 records matched, 114 summaries read, 8 appraised, 106 Not appraised. No included-study table was read for either appraised record: for PMID 33705531 the trial set is Named in the title, and for PMID 30716508 the trial set is recorded as Not read.1

This review was compared against 2 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. The only published synthesis of these two trials avoided the estimand problem this pool has. Joseph et al. pooled individual participant data on ONE outcome defined identically in both trials. This object pools Each trial's own registered primary, and those differ -- which this object's question already states. The comparison therefore does not adjudicate our number; it shows that the literature, given the same two trials, chose a different and more defensible target. Whether to re-pool on A Harmonised outcome is A Content decision and is not made here.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Both contributing trials are keyed to a verified ClinicalTrials.gov registration -- NCT00239681 (JUPITER) and NCT00468923 (HOPE-3) -- and the one comparable synthesis Names both in its title, so the trial-set match is read rather than inferred from participant arithmetic.4
